Public Participation Information

  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution No. 2487, due to the
  continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat
  of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via teleconference. There will not be a physical
  location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 835 0530 6867 Meeting Password: 355733. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 835 0530 6867, Meeting Password: 355733. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  NOVEMBER 15, 2021

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
  Executive Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope,
  Retz, Romanelli,

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT
  MINUTES OF OCTOBER 18, 2021

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  PERISCHINA to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 18, 2021.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   A.  ROCKBLUFF PLAYGROUND PROPOSAL

  Assistant City Manager Davis (ACM) provided a review of the staff report.

  CHAIR POPE opened the floor to Commissioners followed by Community
  Members.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the Play Power quote attachment did not open.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK agreed that his did not open either.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN prefers the Dave Bang Associates quote of what she
  reviewed. ACM Davis shared the Play Power quote on the screen.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if Dave Bang Associates could use the
  swing structure from the Landscape Structures quote if possible. ACM Davis
  responded that it is unlikely to mix vendors and noted the differences between
  vendors and explained that not all companies’ equipment can be equally compared
  due to different pricing structures and warranties associated with the equipment.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the difference of equipment between Dave Bang
  Associates and Landscape Structures is the Tree Trunk structure.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK prefers the Dave Bang Associates swings.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted possible legal restrictions with swapping out
  equipment and wants to defer to the City Attorney for such replacements.

  ACM Davis noted the quote could not be split between two vendors, but the City
  Attorney could be consulted to exchange equipment. She suggested a
  recommendation from the Commission to proceed with Dave Bang Associates as
  a vendor with the lowest dollar quote and then further refined with that company if
  desired.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agreed with COMMISSIONER BAIN that the
  neighborhood was helpful in narrowing down equipment choices. He explained that
  the cost has been a consideration and the allocation of the initial $100,000 was
  observed after receiving initial quotes worth double the amount. He further
  explained that staff has whittled down the project cost to closer match the initial
  budget. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that Dave Bang Associates is his
  recommended company for this project. He believes the extra funds from the ADA
  enhancement is beneficial and votes to proceed with the Dave Bang Associates
  proposal.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if there were more funds available within the ADA
  budget and if it would cover the extra amount in the quotes. ACM Davis noted the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   ADA portion would be covered and the City budgets $40,000 each year for ADA
  enhancements with no specific projects identified. COMMISSIONER RETZ asked
  if this would exhaust the entire ADA budget. ACM Davis noted it would leave about
  $3000 left in the budget but would not deprive other planned projects of funds.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted deciding now while funds are available.

  Community Member Doug Wickstrom, representative of the Rollingwood HOA,
  spoke in favor of the Dave Bang Associates proposal.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION AND PROCEED WITH DAVE BANG
  ASSOCIATES PROPOSAL IN THE AMOUNT OF $137,254.98.

  AYES: Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz,
  Romanelli

  ABSENT: None

  B.  CHANDLER PARK PLAYGROUND SURVEY

  ACM Davis provided a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ agreed with the survey’s questions. CHAIR POPE agreed
  and commended the open-ended questions.

  Community Member Chris Oldroyd noted the exact location of the playground is not
  indicated in the survey, along with the exact footprint including the ADA pathway.
  Mr. Oldroyd continued that the number of play structures is not specified as well;
  The distance from the playground to the bathrooms should also be ADA compliant
  for equal access; total aggregate budget should also be mentioned.

  Community Member Lyneigh Palacios asked how the survey respondent’s
  addresses would be used and if information from the survey would be extracted
  based on those with addresses from a walkable location. She noted wanting to see
  responses separated between those who live within one to two miles walking
  distance and those further away from the park. She explained that asking survey
  takers what school the household children attend may help. She also stated that
  Question #9 could show additional play equipment that was shown in earlier
  surveys or ways to adjust sizes in the question. She suggested that staff speak to
  preschools to help best identify equipment choices. She agreed that ADA concepts
  should be shown in the survey as well.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   ACM Davis noted the site survey will consider an aerial view for the survey, but
  specific equipment will rely on what is recommended. She further explained that for
  more detailed ADA information, the City would need to retain an consultant which
  could be recommended by the Commission if they wished to do so at this stage of
  review. ACM Davis responded that including schools of the children in the survey
  would be helpful.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK agrees with Community Member Oldroyd on
  including the size and scope of the project in the survey. He discourages the use of
  equipment that looks to make a lot of noise like the rocking horse or spinning
  equipment but may consider a small slide. He stated that ADA compliance will occur
  in all locations over time and should not prohibit the project from happening.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI commends staff on the survey and likes the idea
  of a bird’s eye view of the project. He recommends adding a question, why those
  are not in favor of a play area and ask to provide an explanation.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the specifics of play equipment and noted
  going for natural looking pieces. She agreed the site map should be included in the
  survey and that the space should be identified first and then equipment should be
  chosen. ACM Davis clarified that an aerial view be included in the survey.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK agrees with COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
  about adding a question explaining their rejection of play equipment.

  CHAIR POPE noted another draft of the survey be made.

  ACM Davis noted the survey changes would include adding an aerial view of the
  playground which indicates size, dropping the spinning seat and rocking horse,
  considering Bucher Parks equipment in the survey, and adding the follow-up
  question for rejecting a playground option.

  CHAIR POPE directed that this revised survey should be placed on the next agenda
  and thanked the Commission and community members for their feedback.

  C.  PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT

  Management Analyst Slawson provided a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if John Pagliano’s name has come up
  during the project. AMC Davis noted the trail is called the Pagliano trail, but it has
  not yet been formally recognized as such.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the Highridge Park exercise equipment
  could be renovated or removed as well. ACM Davis noted most equipment has

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   been removed from Highridge Park. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted
  one workout station is still available at Ernie Howlett Park as it is still being utilized.
  ACM Davis added that possible grant funding may be available for the exercise
  equipment.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if all the exercise equipment is included in the
  budget. ACM Davis responded that prices have gone up over time and that some
  City funds may be needed. COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the funds for the
  equipment may be better used elsewhere. ACM Davis noted the grant funding from
  2012 was to replace equipment along with the trail improvements; senior adaptive
  equipment is being sought after along with funds from COVID Care to help cover
  the cost of that type of equipment. She suggested a survey may use to gauge
  interest in equipment or if the funds may be applied towards other uses.
  Management Analyst Slawson noted the input and will notify the County
  Administrator on what would be best utilized at those locations.

  ACM Davis noted more information will be provided as the project moves forward.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the trail extends to the back of the tennis courts
  and not the street. Management Analyst Slawson responded it extends from the
  stable area to the back of the arena and will come back with better mapping of the
  project. ACM Davis noted the V-ditch area and the trail that is part of the pathway
  proposed project and that the grant funding only covers the V-ditch area and part
  of the trail.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted it originally went all around the park. ACM
  Davis explained that the V-ditch drainage area is the section in most need of the
  grant funding. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith explained the watershed of
  the park and the settling it causes with causes washout from the arenas and
  overflows over the slope towards Hawthorne due to the V-ditch. COMMISSIONER
  BAIN asked it would be better to move fitness equipment to the other side of the
  park due to flooding concerns. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted that
  the V-ditch portion was most in need of repair and that once the area is repaired
  the equipment placement would not be an issue.

  D.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLE TOURNAMENT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the event was a great success even
  in the off-season and had 137 participants total. Five event sponsors supported the
  event this year with a top tier $2,500 donation from Cal Water.

  COMMISISONER ROMANELLI wanted to congratulate the staff and the transition to
  USTA as recommended by Tracy Austin. He explained that Community Services

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   Supervisor Pinuelas many phone calls and coordination were integral to the
  tournament being held.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK echoed COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI’S
  sentiments and commented on the USTA draw and asked if it was used the whole
  time as Tournament Director Bob Krueger was using paper. Community Services
  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that some directors still use paper to map out their draw,
  but that the USTA site was updated by staff. She explained that Mr. Krueger tracked
  scores on paper while staff inputted scores online. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  asked if runners-up received picture frames as well as champions. Community
  Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted runners-up do receive frames and can be
  contacted if needed. He asked if a package were available for sponsors to easily
  choose which events they would like to sponsor with photos of the events. ACM Davis
  noted the Commission reviewed the sponsorship packet that was developed in early
  2020 and it will be reviewed again and sent out for 2022. She further shared that Ms.
  Austin asked that the Chamber of Commerce participate in in special events sponsor
  recruitment as well. He asked if the NextDoor App was used for sponsorships. ACM
  Davis noted it has not been done but will look to partnering with the Chamber of
  Commerce in the future and social media options

  CHAIR POPE noted social media is a great way to recognize sponsors but may not
  be to procure them. The Planning Committee’s ability to seek out sponsorships should
  also be analyzed.

  ACM Davis added the City Council’s desire for a Pepper Tree Board of Directors to
  form a fundraising committee to help with funding for special events and large capital
  projects.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the Commission could also reach out in an
  organized fashion for sponsorship and explained that the Chamber of Commerce is
  an underutilized resource as they know of potential sponsorships and may want to be
  sponsors themselves.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the business owners that operate outside of
  the City, and that outside businesses and non-brick-and-mortar businesses should be
  considered.

  E.  PARADE OF LIGHTS UPDATE

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the parade was three weeks away
  and that LA Dodger Kenley Jansen would be the Grand Marshall. There were eight
  sponsors at that point for a total of $3,250 in sponsorship fees and that letters to VIP’s
  would be sent out soon.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if there were any plans to remodel the Ernie
  Howlett bathrooms and locker area. He also asked if the bathroom could be
  remodeled to include more restroom facilities by removing the lockersif they are not
  being used since they seem unused. ACM Davis noted no additional funds were
  budgeted this year for that area but could be considered in a future budget year.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the floors were in the process of
  resurfacing and painting. He explained that the lockers have not been utilized much
  and could be open to remodeling and repainting the exterior of the structure is the
  next item on the list for the area.

  ACM Davis noted this item will be brought back in the Spring for a capital project
  review.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the yearly maintenance crew holiday lunch
  and offered to organize it but offered the opportunity to the Commission if anyone
  wished to take it on. The cost would be $10-$12 per Commissioner and would
  consist of purchasing and dropping off the lunch to the crew while offering some
  words of thanks. COMMISSIONER RETZ stated he would not be able available but
  commended Superintendent Goldsmith and his crew. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI took up the task of providing the luncheon.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN is a booster of the South Coast Botanic Garden and
  promoted the Glow Exhibit going on at the Garden. COMMISSIONER RETZ
  echoed those sentiments.

  B.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR POPE and COMMISSIONER RETZ commended  Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith on his work at their respective parks.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted a sign near the George F Canyon Learning
  Tree was damaged and a bench has been dismantled. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith noted the report and stated he would inspect it the
  following day. He also shared that the Nature Trail had been trimmed and would
  continue.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked when work on the Highridge Mural would take place.
  ACM Davis noted that an agreement had been drafted and sent to the artist for
  signature. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted a Mid-March finish time.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted the old shed on the Junior field.
  Maintenance Superintendent responded that it was on the list of items to the sent
  to the Junior League along with Scoreboard sign issues.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that Ernie Howlett Park had a leaky sprinkler
  valve east of the play equipment between the tennis courts and the play equipment,
  a 400-400 square foot area of grass has been soaked. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith is actively working on locating the leak.

  C.  DECEMBER MEETING DATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis asked the Commission if the meeting would still take place next
  month during the Holiday week and recommends cancellation if no matters need
  to be brought forth to the Commission or to move them to the January meeting.

  CHAIR POPE would like to approve the meeting for an alternative date of
  December 13 to review the Chandler Park survey considering the public’s
  comments. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if this would be sent as an
  email or meeting. ACM Davis noted it may be more prudent to review at the
  public meeting in coordination with the Brown Act. COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK noted the survey changes have been addressed and that a
  meeting may not be needed. Since these processes take a while, City Staff may
  not need to come back for that one item. ACM Davis noted the final draft could
  be shared with the Subcommittee before being sent to the public. CHAIR POPE
  asked if the Commission would be able to see it before being sent to the public.
  ACM Davis recommended the survey coming to the full Commission as that is
  what is expected by the public. The meeting could be held in December or
  January.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN agrees with keeping the momentum going and would
  like to address the ADA pathway and work needed to meet ADA compliance.
  The compliance issue should be added to the survey. CHAIR POPE agrees and
  that ADA compliance should be a public matter. She is fine meeting a week prior
  and would be ok with a short meeting in December to keep momentum going.

  ACM Davis recommends rescheduling the regular meeting to December 13,
  2021. All Commissioners agreed.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  None

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
NOVEMBER 15, 2021
   A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF OCTOBER 12, 2021

  Received and filed.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF OCTOBER 26, 2021

  Received and filed.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PETER WEBER CONTRACT RENEWAL

  ACM Davis noted staff is working with Peter Weber. The contract ends November
  30th and stormwater issues are being worked out, but the Contract is going to
  continue on a month-to-month basis until some items are

  B.  TENNIS COURT RENOVATION

  ACM Davis will bring the item to the Commission before City Council.

  C.  PICKLEBALL USAGE

  ACM Davis noted staff is trying to ramp up use to bring a thorough report back to
  the Commission.

  CHAIR POPE asked about the snow day. ACM Davis noted the item did not go to
  the City Council yet and staff is still working on the details of the event for a January
  date.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:51 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON DECEMBER 13,
  2021 AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD VIA TELECONFERENCE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,
